messages:
maria: Hey @eng-runtime — I hit a regression on the LLM inference bench. I captured an nsys trace (out.qdrep), a torch.profiler dump (profile.ptl), and a small TorchScript model. Need tips for safely sharing this with the team (remove hostnames, strip weights/KV cache, shrink file size). I put raw traces at s3://redwood-internal/traces/1791/reg1/ but it contains hostnames.

jack: For sharing, strip model weights and KV cache for sure. nsys QDREP is binary — export summaries first: `nsys stats -r 1 -f csv out.qdrep -o out_stats` then scrub CSV. If you can reproduce a smaller trace (shorter seq / smaller batch) that helps.

li: If possible, reproduce with `--max-batch 1 --seq-len 128` to keep traces small. Also run torch.profiler with `with_stack=True` so we get stack traces in the exported report.

oliver: We have an internal helper: `trace-uploader` (infra-tools). It can sanitize env vars and strip weights: `trace-uploader sanitize --remove-env HOSTNAME,USER --strip-weights --strip-kvcache --output trace_sanitized.zip out.qdrep profile.ptl model.ptl`.

maria: Great — where's `trace-uploader`? binary or repo?

sam: It's in infra-tools: https://git.redwood/tools/trace-uploader. If you don't have access, upload to a signed URL and ping me; I can run sanitization and re-upload.

deploy-bot: FYI raw traces sometimes include `/etc/hosts` entries and shell env dumps. Be careful with IPs and hostnames. Consider removing those before sharing. :warning:

ash: Instead of editing system files, you can export nsys to a text format and scrub host lines: `nsys export --format=console --output out.txt out.qdrep` then `grep -vE "(hostname|10\.|172\.|192\.)" out.txt > out_sanitized.txt`.

maria: Here's the command I'm using to capture: ```nsys profile -o out -t cuda,osrt --trace=nvtx,osrt python run_bench.py && nsys stats out.qdrep --format csv -o out_stats``` Anything missing I should add?

jack: Add a focused capture window so you don't include startup noise: start trace right before inference and stop after. Also export the flamegraph: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx --output out --export=flamegraph` (if your nsys supports it) or use `nsys stats` CSV -> flamegraph tool.

oliver: When you share, include a `run_config.yaml` with: GPU type, CUDA/cuDNN versions, torch commit hash, model checksum (not the weights), run args, and host instance type. That helps reproduce locally.

maria: I ran the sanitizer and used the uploader. Uploaded sanitized zip to https://s3.redwood/traces/1791004800/maria_reg_sanitized.zip (IAM-restricted). I also attached `run_config.yaml` inside the zip. Ping me if you need access.

sam: I have access and pulled it. Quick glance: there's a small perf bump at step 3 of the run. I'll try to repro with the smaller seq/batch and open a tiny PR to add extra timing hooks.

li: If we need deeper NVTX/Nsys-level info we might ask for ephemeral creds to get the full .qdrep — but try the exported flamegraphs & CSV first. 9/10 we can triage from that.

oliver: :thumbsup: Thanks @maria. If you want, we can pair for 15 mins later to look at KV cache usage; I can bring a small script to visualize token-level timing.

maria: Thanks all — will run the smaller repro, confirm the trimmed traces, and ping @oliver for pairing if the flamegraphs don't explain it.
